# VibePascal v58 -- cross-platform status manifest
# Cut by FPCDeveloper (Otto).  win64 + linux64 shipped 2026-09-11 (cy1117);
# i386-linux-cross, arm-linux-cross, aarch64-linux and arm-linux shipped
# 2026-09-11 (cy1118); x86_64-darwin and aarch64-darwin shipped 2026-09-11
# (cy1119).  v58 is now on EVERY target this fork publishes.  The section at
# the end records that the macOS pair shipped hours after the rest, and why,
# rather than quietly erasing the gap.
# This file is the authoritative answer to "which platforms have v58".
# Per-platform detail lives in dist/<target>/VERSION.txt and inside each tarball.
# There is no RELEASE-v57.txt: v57 shipped to win64 and linux64 only, and every
# target that skipped it collects it here, so v57 is documented below too.

source_commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
compiler_fix:  dedf242c69  (compiler/entfile.pas -- tppufile.readheader)
parent:        v57 (1f605f41b3b06a5fa84fb4cb31ee4298fb30907f, fix c31227c8ca)

WHAT CHANGED IN v57 AND v58 -- ONE ACCIDENT, TWO BYTES APART
  Both fixes are about the same thing happening to a unit file: a killed build,
  a full disk or an interrupted copy leaves a .ppu HALF WRITTEN.

  v57 (c31227c8ca)  A short read inside the .ppu reader is now an error.  Before
                    it, a half-written unit could put the compiler into an
                    infinite 99%-CPU spin with no message at all -- you had to
                    notice a build that never ended and go looking.

  v58 (dedf242c69)  v57 only ever noticed damage it happened to trip over.  Lose
                    the TAIL of a unit and there is nothing to trip over, because
                    nothing an interface load reads lives in the last handful of
                    bytes: the compiler read what it wanted, never reached the
                    missing part, and built your program against a unit that is
                    not all there.  Exit 0, no message, nothing to search a log
                    for.  Measured on a real 55291-byte unit, every truncation
                    from 55271 bytes upward was accepted.
                    A .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete
                    file is always 40 bytes of header plus that number and can
                    never be fewer.  tppufile.readheader now compares the two and
                    rejects a SHORT file.  Longer than declared stays legal, as
                    it always was.  The arithmetic is 64-bit on purpose: the
                    declared size is an unsigned 32-bit field, and a corrupt
                    header claiming near 4 GB would wrap a 32-bit sum and switch
                    the check off at exactly the moment it is needed.

  THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing: a
  truncated unit whose source is available is RECOMPILED and the build goes
  green; a good copy of the same unit in a later -Fu directory is used instead;
  only a truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and
  it stops with the message an absent unit already gives.  Nobody is ever told to
  go and delete a file.

  COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY.  No PPU FORMAT change -- the reader got stricter, the
  format did not move -- and no RTL or package change, so existing unit sets stay
  valid on every platform.

HOW EACH BINARY WAS SHOWN TO CARRY THE FIX -- AND WHY NOT BY VERSION STRING
  Every one of these compilers reports "3.3.1".  The version string cannot tell
  v54 from v58, so it was never used as evidence.  The discriminating test is
  dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh: truncate a REAL .ppu for that target at 25
  offsets and score what the compiler does, with the unit in exactly ONE
  directory and its source off every search path -- otherwise a correct rejection
  resolves from a shadow copy and reads as a pass.

  Each new binary was run against the PRESERVED binary it replaces, the one that
  actually shipped, re-run this cycle rather than argued from source:

    target             replaced binary        pre-fix           post-fix
    i386-linux         ppcross386  v54        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    arm-linux (cross)  ppcrossarm  v54        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    aarch64-linux      ppca64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    arm-linux (native) ppcarm      v56        12/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    x86_64-darwin      ppcx64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0
    aarch64-darwin     ppca64      v56        11/25, exit 1     25/25, exit 0

  THE TWO DARWIN ROWS ARE NOT THE SHIPPED MACH-O BINARIES, and saying so is the
  point.  Nothing here can execute a Mach-O, so those two lines were measured on
  Linux-hosted compilers built from the SAME source commit, targeting darwin and
  reading real <arch>-darwin .ppu files.  They are evidence about the SOURCE the
  shipped binaries were built from, not about the shipped binaries running.  What
  ties the source to the bytes is the section triage in the darwin VERSION.txt
  files: v56 source vs v58 source, both cross-built here today with the same host
  compiler, RTL and flags, __text +896 (x86_64) and +784 (aarch64), against a
  build-noise floor of SEVENTEEN BYTES of LC_UUID on the Intel side and identical
  section sizes on the arm64 side.

  The pre-fix failures split into a loud half and a silent half: 8 or 9 offsets
  HUNG and had to be killed at 30 seconds, and 5 were ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a
  corrupt unit taken as valid, which is the half v58 exists for.  The native arm
  compiler scores 13 problems where its cross twin scores 14; one offset that
  spins on the host binary errors out on the native one.  That is reported as
  measured rather than rounded to match, and the silent five are identical on
  every target.

A CROSS BUILD CAN LIE ABOUT BEING ONE -- CHECK THE UNIT COUNT, NOT THE HASH
  Recorded because it nearly shipped four stale compilers with fresh hashes.
  The first ppcross386 build this cycle compiled ONE file (pp.pas, 795 lines),
  never touched the patched entfile.pas, reused units from 2026-09-03 for
  everything else -- and emitted a NEW md5, which reads exactly like a successful
  rebuild.  A separate incremental arm build did worse: it crashed the driver
  compiler with an access violation.  Both were cured by wiping
  compiler/<target>/{bin,units} and rebuilding from scratch, with no source
  change.  Units recompiled per binary this release: 277 (i386), 223 (aarch64),
  241 (arm), 250 (x86_64-darwin), 223 (aarch64-darwin).  If you
  reproduce these, assert that count.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-11 (cy1119): THE MACOS PAIR SHIPPED, HOURS AFTER THE REST
  Both darwin targets now carry v58 and are listed above.  The paragraph below is
  left exactly as it was written earlier today, because it is the record of what
  this manifest said while the gap was open -- not because it is still true.  The
  one line in it that is now WRONG is "STILL ON v56"; everything it says about
  WHY the darwin delivery path is different is still correct and is why those two
  entries carry an extra SIGNING note and no runtime claim.

  Still true after this addendum, and the reason the honesty section above is
  worded the way it is: v58 is on every target, but the macOS pair is the only
  one where nobody has ever executed the shipped binary.

--- SUPERSEDED, KEPT VERBATIM (written 2026-09-11, cy1118) ---
STILL ON v56 AFTER THIS RELEASE
  x86_64-darwin/   vibepascal-v56-a187bbac34-x86_64-darwin-bin.tar.gz
  aarch64-darwin/  vibepascal-v56-a187bbac34-aarch64-darwin-bin.tar.gz

  Both macOS targets are missing v57 AND v58.  On those compilers a half-written
  unit still hangs forever and a tail-truncated one is still taken as valid.
  Nobody is blocked on anybody: it is a build step, and darwin is NOT blocked on
  a missing SDK (pass -XR to mac_sdk/MacOSX26.2.sdk and both darwin targets
  link).  It is deliberately NOT bundled into this release because the darwin
  delivery path is different: build-release.sh ad-hoc signs every bundled Mach-O
  with rcodesign, a signature APPENDS bytes and CHANGES the hash, so publishing
  an unsigned staging hash there is the exact thing that reads to a careful user
  as corruption.  See the signing sections of dist/RELEASE-v56.txt before
  attempting it.  Tracked on the open ledger row darwin_stale_v58.

  Do not read this manifest as "the fix is everywhere".  It is on every Linux and
  Windows target and on neither macOS target.
